newsitem.title: USA: Valujet to buy AirWays, will drop name.
newsitem.headline: Valujet to buy AirWays, will drop name.

text.p: The ValuJet Airlines name, indelibly linked to an airplane's deadly plunge into the Florida Everglades, is to disappear with the purchase by ValuJet Inc. of AirWays Corp., announced Thursday.
In a deal worth about $62 million, the two airlines said they will form a new holding company that will be called AirTran Holdings Inc.
ValuJet has struggled to regain passengers and make money since its Atlanta-bound Flight 592 crashed shortly after takeoff from Miami on May 11, 1996, killing all 110 passengers and crew on board.
ValuJet President Joseph Corr and AirWays Chairman Robert Swenson told a news conference that they agreed to the merger because it made good economic sense.
However, Corr acknowledged the likely merits of dropping the ValuJet name.
"The merger is driven by the economic side. Make no mistake about that," Corr said. "By putting the two companies together it is much more viable economically."
But he said that the AirTran name "offers us a much better opportunity of going forward. It basically came down to one name or another. We felt AirTran better represented the newness of the company."

The combined company will serve 46 cities with 238 flights daily, a fleet of 40 aircraft and 2,742 employees. "We both emphasise affordable fares. We will continue to bring affordable fares to the people of this nation," Swenson said.

Alan Siegel of the New York-based marketing company Siegel and Gale said the name change was an important move by Valujet. "It seems to me ValuJet didn't have a chance of succeeding if they kept the name. By merging they have rational for changing the name without it looking like a knee-jerk reaction."

The deal calls for ValuJet, based in Atlanta, to acquire Orlando-based AirWays in a stock swap. To carry out the swap, ValuJet will issue about 9.1 million shares of stock worth $62 million based on Wednesday's closing price of $6.81 a share.
AirWays spokesman Eric Hobson said other assets would be involved in the deal, but he did not put a value on them. The deal is meant to be tax free to shareholders.

The Everglades disaster raised numerous questions about ValuJet's safety procedures. Preliminary reports indicated the crash was caused by a fire in the cargo hold ignited by oxygen-generating canisters that had been mislabeled and improperly secured. The National Transportation Safety Board's final report is expected later this month.

AirWays' AirTran Airways currently provides service between Orlando and 23 cities with a fleet of Boeing 737 aircraft. It expects delivery of its 11th plane this month. ValuJet operates to 24 cities with a fleet of 30 aircraft.
Corr, who joined ValuJet last November, will serve as president and chief executive officer. Swenson, now CEO and chairman at Airways, will become non-executive chairman.
Corr said he did not expect many job losses because neither company is overstaffed.
Both carriers will continue to function under their respective operating certificates, the companies said.

The merger is expected to close in three to four months. The company will initially be based in Orlando, where AirWays has maintenance facilities, and the Florida city is a leading candidate for its permanent base.
AirWays' stock rose $1.25 to $6.625, while ValueJet added 50 cents to $7.31, both on Nasdaq.
